name: Plastic bottle
preparation: Empty the bottle, remove the cap and label if your local rules require it, and rinse it lightly.
disposal: Put it in the plastic recycling collection. Keep it separate from general waste.
tip: Do not put a bottle with leftover liquid into the recycling bin.

name: Plastic food container
preparation: Remove food and rinse the container. Check the recycling symbol and local rules.
disposal: Place clean accepted plastic containers in the plastic recycling collection.
tip: Heavily contaminated or mixed-material containers may not be accepted.

name: Plastic bag
preparation: Keep it clean and dry. Do not mix it with rigid plastic items unless local guidance says so.
disposal: Follow your local collection rules. Some areas have a separate bag or film collection; otherwise use the designated waste stream.
tip: Plastic film can become tangled in sorting machines, so check local guidance first.

name: Paper
preparation: Keep paper clean and dry. Remove plastic covers and other non-paper materials.
disposal: Put it in the paper recycling collection.
tip: Wet, oily, or food-soiled paper is often not accepted with clean paper.

name: Cardboard box
preparation: Flatten the box and remove tape or plastic wrapping where practical.
disposal: Place it in the paper/cardboard recycling collection.
tip: Keep cardboard dry and free from food residue.

name: Newspaper
preparation: Keep newspapers clean and dry. Bundle them if required by your local collection.
tip: Do not include tissues or heavily soiled paper.

name: Glass bottle
preparation: Empty and rinse the bottle. Separate caps or lids according to local rules.
disposal: Put it in the glass recycling collection, using the correct color section if your area separates colors.
tip: Broken glass may require special handling; follow local safety and collection guidance.

name: Glass jar
preparation: Empty and rinse the jar. Remove the lid if required.
disposal: Place it in the glass recycling collection.
tip: Ceramics, mirrors, and heat-resistant glass are usually not accepted with bottle glass.

name: Aluminum can
preparation: Empty and rinse the can. Do not crush it if your local collection asks you to keep its shape.
disposal: Put it in the metal or can recycling collection.
tip: Make sure no liquid remains inside.

name: Steel food can
preparation: Empty, rinse, and drain the can. Handle sharp edges carefully.
disposal: Place it in the metal recycling collection.
tip: Check local guidance for attached lids.

name: Food waste
preparation: Drain excess liquid and remove packaging, plastic, and other contaminants.
disposal: Use the designated food-waste collection or composting system.
tip: Rules differ by area; check which food scraps are accepted.

name: Used tissue
disposal: Put it in general waste unless your local authority provides a separate accepted stream.
tip: Used tissues are generally not accepted with clean paper recycling.

name: Ceramic cup
preparation: Wrap broken pieces securely and follow local disposal guidance.
disposal: Do not put ceramics in bottle-glass recycling. Use the designated waste route.
tip: Ceramic and porcelain have different properties from container glass.

name: Battery
preparation: Keep batteries out of ordinary trash. Protect terminals if local guidance recommends it.
disposal: Take them to an approved battery collection point.
tip: Never place batteries in regular recycling or general waste when a collection point is available.
